items.b: 999.46 IN SHANGHAI, FIFTY-FOUR FEN SHORT OF A ROUND NUMBER
items.t: The Shanghai Gold Exchange's Au(T+D) was quoted at 999.46 yuan a gram on 22 August, up 20.19 yuan or 2.06% from a close of 979.27. This paper printed the same contract at 940.44 on 14 August, so the exchange leg has run 6.28% in eight sessions.

items.b: THREE CHINESE COUNTERS PRICED THE SAME NIGHT THREE DIFFERENT WAYS
items.t: Lao Miao Gold moved its board to 1,391 yuan a gram, up 34; Lao Feng Xiang to 1,388, up 32; Chow Sang Sang to 1,387, up 22. That is 2.51%, 2.36% and 1.61% against each brand's own previous board. Two beat the exchange's 2.06%, one trailed it.

items.b: THE SATURDAY PRICE TABLES CARRY FRIDAY'S COUNTER BOARD
items.t: Chinese roundups datestamped 22 August at 07:00 put the exchange's Saturday quotation beside counter figures of 1,365, 1,363 and 1,356. Those back-solve to Friday. A markup read off one of those tables is measured across two sessions and prints too low.

items.b: NO METAL WAS WRITTEN BACK TO THE TAPE THIS MORNING
items.t: The Editor re-read Kitco at press time on Sunday. Gold $4,602.40 and silver $68.86, identical to the 05:00 mark, no session having opened since Friday. Platinum stays at $1,881.00, the last mark both pages agreed on, with Kitco and TradingEconomics 0.99% apart.

items.b: ISRAEL'S HALF-YEAR BREAKS INTO FOUR LEGS FOR THE FIRST TIME
items.t: Net polished exports $625.7m, down 22.3%; net polished imports $531.3m, down 12.7%; net rough exports $191.2m, down 34.6%; net rough imports $208.3m, down 35.8%. Published 16 August by Emess. Rapaport carries the polished export figure at the same level.

items.b: ROUGH FELL 1.94 TIMES AS FAST AS POLISHED IN ISRAEL
items.t: Grouped by category, the two rough legs fell 35.3% and the two polished legs 18.1%. Rough intake is a cutting centre's order book, and it leads polished output by six to twelve months. Rough imports were 40.3% of polished exports a year ago and are 33.3% now.

items.b: CORRECTION: DVASH IS NOT CHAIRMAN OF THE IDI OR THE IDE
items.t: Saturday's article said Yoram Dvash remains chairman of the Israel Diamond Institute and the Israel Diamond Exchange. He was previously chairman of both, as the Rapaport report cited beside the claim states. Corrected on the page, in the record and in the panel.

items.b: CORRECTION: 14.9 TONNES A DAY ON MCX IS VOLUME, NOT TURNOVER
items.t: Saturday's India article and its panel labelled 14.9 tonnes as MCX average daily turnover. The World Gold Council reports it as average daily trading volume, up from 13.5 tonnes, and reports turnover separately at 214 billion rupees, about $2.2 billion, up 9%.

items.b: WATCHES GOES DARK A THIRD CONSECUTIVE EDITION
items.t: The watches desk re-checked all five standing anchors and filed genuinely dry. The Swiss federation's next export print is due 17 September and the earnings calendar is exhausted. Three dark editions running is the threshold at which this becomes a structural question.
